title: Asbestos scope, definitions, classes of work and exposure limits practice questions
description: Practice questions on OSHA's construction asbestos rule: scope, ACM and PACM, Class I-IV work, key terms, exposure and multi-employer duties.

questions.question: A crew on a construction site is applying an asbestos-containing asphalt roof coating. What does 1926.1101(a)(8) say about this material?

options.A: It is Class II asbestos work
options.B: The section does not apply to asbestos-containing asphalt roof coatings
options.C: It must be treated as PACM
options.D: It is covered only if the coating is friable

questions.explanation: Paragraph (a)(8) states: "This section does not apply to asbestos-containing asphalt roof coatings, cements and mastics."
questions.evidence: This section does not apply to asbestos-containing asphalt roof coatings, cements and mastics.

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(a)(7), what is coverage under the asbestos standard based on?

options.A: The employer's industry classification code
options.B: The number of employees on the site
options.C: The dollar value of the construction contract
options.D: The nature of the work operation involving asbestos exposure

questions.explanation: Paragraph (a)(7) states: "Coverage under this standard shall be based on the nature of the work operation involving asbestos exposure."
questions.evidence: Coverage under this standard shall be based on the nature of the work operation involving asbestos exposure.

questions.question: How does 1926.1101(b) define presumed asbestos containing material (PACM)?

options.A: Thermal system insulation and surfacing material found in buildings constructed no later than 1980
options.B: Any building material installed before 1980 that has not been sampled
options.C: Any material containing more than one percent asbestos
options.D: Floor tile and roofing found in buildings constructed no later than 1980

questions.explanation: The rule defines it as "thermal system insulation and surfacing material found in buildings constructed no later than 1980." Any material containing more than one percent asbestos is the definition of ACM, not PACM.
questions.evidence: Presumed Asbestos Containing Material means thermal system insulation and surfacing material found in buildings constructed no later than 1980.

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(b), what makes a material asbestos-containing material (ACM)?

options.A: It contains any detectable amount of asbestos
options.B: It contains more than 0.1 percent asbestos
options.C: It contains more than one percent asbestos
options.D: It contains more than 5 percent asbestos

questions.explanation: The rule states: "Asbestos-containing material (ACM), means any material containing more than one percent asbestos."
questions.evidence: Asbestos-containing material (ACM), means any material containing more than one percent asbestos.

questions.question: Which description matches "surfacing material" as defined in 1926.1101(b)?

options.A: Material bonded into a matrix that cannot be crumbled by hand
options.B: Material that is sprayed, troweled-on or otherwise applied to surfaces
options.C: ACM applied to pipes, boilers and ducts to prevent heat loss or gain
options.D: Any material attached to a load-supporting structural member

questions.explanation: Surfacing material "means material that is sprayed, troweled-on or otherwise applied to surfaces", such as acoustical plaster on ceilings and fireproofing materials on structural members. ACM applied to pipes, boilers and ducts to prevent heat loss or gain is thermal system insulation.
questions.evidence: Surfacing material means material that is sprayed, troweled-on or otherwise applied to surfaces

questions.question: A contractor is removing asbestos-containing floor tile from a corridor. Under 1926.1101(b), which class of asbestos work is this?

options.A: Class I
options.B: Class III
options.C: Class IV
options.D: Class II

questions.explanation: Class II work is "the removal of ACM which is not thermal system insulation or surfacing material", and the rule says "This includes, but is not limited to, the removal of asbestos-containing wallboard, floor tile and sheeting".
questions.evidence: This includes, but is not limited to, the removal of asbestos-containing wallboard, floor tile and sheeting, roofing and siding shingles, and construction mastics.

questions.question: A custodial employee cleans up dust and debris left from a completed Class I job. Under 1926.1101(b), which class of asbestos work is this cleanup?

options.A: Class I
options.B: Class II
options.C: Class IV
options.D: Class III

questions.explanation: Class IV work includes "activities to clean up dust, waste and debris resulting from Class I, II, and III activities."
questions.evidence: activities to clean up dust, waste and debris resulting from Class I, II, and III activities.

questions.question: A maintenance worker is repairing a valve, without removing any insulation, in a spot where thermal system insulation ACM is likely to be disturbed. Under 1926.1101(b), which class of asbestos work is this?

options.A: Class III
options.B: Class I
options.C: Class II
options.D: Class IV

questions.explanation: Class III work "means repair and maintenance operations, where “ACM”, including TSI and surfacing ACM and PACM, is likely to be disturbed." Class I is the removal of TSI and surfacing ACM and PACM.
questions.evidence: Class III asbestos work means repair and maintenance operations, where “ACM”, including TSI and surfacing ACM and PACM, is likely to be disturbed.

questions.topic: Work terms: disturbance, removal and repair
questions.question: Under the 1926.1101(b) definition of disturbance, what limit is placed on the amount of ACM or PACM disturbed?

options.A: No more than one 55-gallon drum of waste per shift
options.B: No more than 10 square feet per work area per day
options.C: No more than the competent person approves in writing
options.D: No more than can be contained in one glove bag or waste bag not exceeding 60 inches in length and width

questions.explanation: The definition states: "In no event shall the amount of ACM or PACM so disturbed exceed that which can be contained in one glove bag or waste bag which shall not exceed 60 inches in length and width."
questions.evidence: In no event shall the amount of ACM or PACM so disturbed exceed that which can be contained in one glove bag or waste bag which shall not exceed 60 inches in length and width.

questions.topic: Work terms: disturbance, removal and repair
questions.question: Under 1926.1101(b), encapsulation of ACM attached to a structure falls within which defined term?

options.A: Repair
options.B: Removal
options.C: Demolition
options.D: Aggressive method

questions.explanation: Repair means overhauling, rebuilding, reconstructing, or reconditioning of structures or substrates, "including encapsulation or other repair of ACM or PACM attached to structures or substrates."
questions.evidence: including encapsulation or other repair of ACM or PACM attached to structures or substrates.

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(b), a regulated area covers the area where Class I, II, and III asbestos work is conducted and what other area?

options.A: Every room on the same floor of the building
options.B: Any area within 25 feet of the work
options.C: Any adjoining area where debris and waste from such asbestos work accumulate
options.D: Any area where Class IV work is conducted

questions.explanation: A regulated area is "an area established by the employer to demarcate areas where Class I, II, and III asbestos work is conducted, and any adjoining area where debris and waste from such asbestos work accumulate".
questions.evidence: an area established by the employer to demarcate areas where Class I, II, and III asbestos work is conducted, and any adjoining area where debris and waste from such asbestos work accumulate

questions.question: In the decontamination area defined in 1926.1101(b), which room has facilities for the storage of employees' street clothing?

options.A: The equipment room
options.B: The clean room
options.C: The shower area
options.D: The regulated area

questions.explanation: "Clean room means an uncontaminated room having facilities for the storage of employees' street clothing and uncontaminated materials and equipment." The equipment room is a contaminated room for disposal of contaminated protective clothing and equipment.
questions.evidence: Clean room means an uncontaminated room having facilities for the storage of employees' street clothing and uncontaminated materials and equipment.

questions.question: For Class III and Class IV work, how does 1926.1101(b) say the competent person is trained?

options.A: In a course meeting EPA's Model Accreditation Plan criteria for supervisor
options.B: By certification from the American Board of Industrial Hygiene
options.C: By completing the training for an abatement project designer
options.D: In a manner consistent with EPA requirements for training of local education agency maintenance and custodial staff

questions.explanation: For Class III and Class IV work the competent person is one "who is trained in a manner consistent with EPA requirements for training of local education agency maintenance and custodial staff as set forth at 40 CFR 763.92 (a)(2)." The Model Accreditation Plan supervisor course applies to Class I and Class II work.
questions.evidence: for Class III and Class IV work, who is trained in a manner consistent with EPA requirements for training of local education agency maintenance and custodial staff as set forth at 40 CFR 763.92 (a)(2).

questions.question: A company leases a building and controls its management and record keeping functions. Which description of "building/facility owner" in 1926.1101(b) fits this company?

options.A: The legal entity, including a lessee, which exercises control over management and record keeping functions
options.B: Only the holder of the recorded deed to the property
options.C: The general contractor on any project in the building
options.D: The competent person assigned to the building

questions.explanation: The rule says "Building/facility owner is the legal entity, including a lessee, which exercises control over management and record keeping functions relating to a building and/or facility" in which activities covered by the standard take place.
questions.evidence: Building/facility owner is the legal entity, including a lessee, which exercises control over management and record keeping functions relating to a building and/or facility

questions.question: An employee wears a respirator during asbestos work. Under 1926.1101(b), what does "employee exposure" mean?

options.A: The concentration measured inside the respirator facepiece
options.B: The exposure to airborne asbestos that would occur if the employee were not using respiratory protective equipment
options.C: The exposure reduced by the respirator's protection factor
options.D: The average concentration in the clean room

questions.explanation: "Employee exposure means that exposure to airborne asbestos that would occur if the employee were not using respiratory protective equipment."
questions.evidence: Employee exposure means that exposure to airborne asbestos that would occur if the employee were not using respiratory protective equipment.

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(b), what does a negative initial exposure assessment demonstrate?

options.A: That no asbestos is present in the building
options.B: That one past air sample was below the PELs
options.C: That employee exposure during an operation is expected to be consistently below the PELs
options.D: That all employees in the area wear respirators

questions.explanation: It is "a demonstration by the employer, which complies with the criteria in paragraph (f)(2)(iii) of this section, that employee exposure during an operation is expected to be consistently below the PELs."
questions.evidence: that employee exposure during an operation is expected to be consistently below the PELs.

questions.question: On a multi-employer worksite, who does 1926.1101(d)(2) say shall abate asbestos hazards?

options.A: The building/facility owner
options.B: The general contractor in every case
options.C: Each employer whose employees are nearby
options.D: The contractor who created or controls the source of asbestos contamination

questions.explanation: "Asbestos hazards at a multi-employer work site shall be abated by the contractor who created or controls the source of asbestos contamination."
questions.evidence: Asbestos hazards at a multi-employer work site shall be abated by the contractor who created or controls the source of asbestos contamination.

questions.question: Employees working immediately adjacent to a Class I job are exposed to asbestos because the job's containment is inadequate. Under the example in 1926.1101(d)(3), which is one of the options their employer shall take?

options.A: Remove the employees from the area until the enclosure breach is repaired
options.B: Have its own employees repair the other contractor's enclosure
options.C: Keep working until the next daily check of the enclosure
options.D: Leave all action to the primary asbestos contractor

questions.explanation: Their employer "shall either remove the employees from the area until the enclosure breach is repaired; or perform an initial exposure assessment pursuant to (f) of this section."
questions.evidence: their employer shall either remove the employees from the area until the enclosure breach is repaired; or perform an initial exposure assessment pursuant to (f) of this section.

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(d)(4), what must employers of employees working adjacent to another employer's regulated area take steps on a daily basis to ascertain?

options.A: The asbestos content of every material in the regulated area
options.B: The integrity of the enclosure and/or the effectiveness of the control method relied on by the primary asbestos contractor
options.C: The training records of the primary asbestos contractor's workers
options.D: The air monitoring results inside the regulated area

questions.explanation: They "shall take steps on a daily basis to ascertain the integrity of the enclosure and/or the effectiveness of the control method relied on by the primary asbestos contractor to assure that asbestos fibers do not migrate to such adjacent areas."
questions.evidence: shall take steps on a daily basis to ascertain the integrity of the enclosure and/or the effectiveness of the control method relied on by the primary asbestos contractor to assure that asbestos fibers do not migrate to such adjacent areas.

questions.question: The general contractor on a project that includes asbestos work is not qualified to serve as the asbestos competent person. Under 1926.1101(d)(5), what shall it do as supervisor of the entire project?

options.A: Serve as the competent person for all Class I work
options.B: Repair every enclosure breach on the site itself
options.C: Ascertain whether the asbestos contractor is in compliance and require it to come into compliance when necessary
options.D: Perform all air monitoring for the asbestos contractor

questions.explanation: "As supervisor of the entire project, the general contractor shall ascertain whether the asbestos contractor is in compliance with this standard, and shall require such contractor to come into compliance with this standard when necessary."
questions.evidence: As supervisor of the entire project, the general contractor shall ascertain whether the asbestos contractor is in compliance with this standard, and shall require such contractor to come into compliance with this standard when necessary.
